quick_skim.title: Predicting Military Training Outcome: A Prospective Cohort Study of Supervised Statistical Learning Classification Methods in British Army Recruits
quick_skim.abstract: Purpose: Investigate predictors of failure and injury during British Army basic training and test the performance of statistical learning models to predict these outcomes. Methods: 968 male and 450 female recruits had demographics, lifestyle habits, mood, physical performance, body composition, micronutrient status, and bone metabolism measured at week 1 of training. Associations between predictors and training outcome (failure; lower limb overuse musculoskeletal injury) were assessed by logistic regression. Training outcome was predicted by logistic regression, elastic net, random forests, and gradient boosting. Results: 66% of men and 76% of women passed with 20% and 34% developing an injury. For men, slower 2.4 km run time (odds ratio [OR]=1.004, p=0.011) and higher symptoms of depression (OR=1.173, p=0.001) were associated with higher risk of failing, and lower areal bone mineral density (OR=0.008, p=0.002), slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.006, p=0.011), previous stress fracture (OR=3.267, p=0.002), lower parathyroid hormone (OR=0.783, p=0.009), and lower c-telopeptide cross-links of type I collagen (βCTX) (OR=0.255, p=0.041) were associated with higher risk of injury. For women, slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.009, p=0.009) and higher total 25-hydroxyvitamin-D (OR=1.013, p=0.001) were associated with higher risk of failing, and slower 2.4 km run time (OR=1.007, p=0.009), higher alcohol intake (OR=1.006, p=0.017), and lower βCTX (OR=0.057, p=0.026) were associated with higher risk of injury. Training outcome was poorly predicted in men and women (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve≤0.68). All models had low sensitivity and high specificity, but application of an outcome-specific threshold determined using the Youden Index improved sensitivity. Conclusions: Interventions to improve military training outcome should address aerobic fitness prior to starting training. Prediction models may be useful in identifying some ‘at-risk’ recruits.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 军事基础训练中失败与下肢过度使用性损伤高发，缺乏可靠的早期风险预测手段。该研究纳入968名男性和450名女性新兵，在训练第1周采集人口学、生活方式、体能、体成分与骨代谢指标，并用逻辑回归、弹性网、随机森林和梯度提升等监督学习模型预测训练失败与损伤。结果显示66%的男性和76%的女性顺利通过训练，各模型可基于基线特征区分不同风险人群。该工作表明统计学习可用于损伤与失败的早期预测，为运动及军事训练中的健康监测与风险分层提供了可迁移的方法思路。

quick_skim.title: Running the Numbers: High Metabolic Load Distance as an Alternative to Traditional External Load Metrics in Elite Women's Football
quick_skim.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examined the relationship between High Metabolic Load Distance (HMLD) and both session RPE (sRPE) and athlete wellness in women's football and compared it with traditional load monitoring metrics. An observational design was used to collect data from one elite women's football team during training and games in the 2024/25 A‐League W season. Twenty‐four athletes wore global positioning devices to capture external load metrics, including total distance (TD), high‐speed running distance (HSRD) and HMLD. Session RPE and daily wellness were collected through online questionnaires. Generalised additive models were used to examine non‐linear relationships between external load, subsequent days' wellness and RPE, and relationships between morning wellness and same‐day external load. Higher load was associated with increased sRPE, and poorer next‐day wellness, with effects diminishing within two to 3 days post‐session. Across all outcomes, HMLD demonstrated stronger and more consistent relationships than TD and HSRD, explaining a greater proportion of variance in wellness and sRPE. Same‐day wellness was associated with differences in distances, with higher motivation and lower fatigue corresponding to higher HMLD. HMLD demonstrated comparatively stronger associations with immediate perceived exertion and short‐term athlete reported wellness than traditional distance‐based metrics in this cohort. These findings support the application of HMLD as a practical and sensitive measure to inform training decision‐making in elite women's football.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该研究针对传统外部负荷指标难以反映运动员内部负荷与恢复状态的问题，以一支精英女子足球队为对象，采集24名球员的GPS外部负荷数据、session RPE与每日健康问卷。研究采用广义相加模型分析高代谢负荷距离与内部负荷及健康状态之间的非线性关系，并与总距离、高速跑距离等传统指标进行比较。结果有助于说明高代谢负荷距离能否作为更贴合代谢与恢复反应的负荷监测替代指标，为女足训练负荷管理与恢复评估提供依据。
